title: SLO-driven pricing + latency claims — hypotheses & benchmark plan
content:
Purpose:
Quick working paper to align the performance claims (latency) we want to take to market with a companion SLO-driven pricing angle. This is intentionally hypothesis-first — we will iterate with engineering benchmarks and sales feedback before final copy.

Top-level thesis (one line):
Customers buy predictable latency and predictable cost: convert that into SLO-backed pricing tiers and a small set of provable claims (p50/p95/p99) that map to unit economics per 1M tokens.

What we want to test / claim candidates:
- Claim A (conservative): "p95 infer latency <= 250ms for conversational workloads at 32 token/sec request pacing on Dedicated instances" — backed by three internal runs and one customer-staging run.
- Claim B (aggressive): "Average token cost 15% lower than MajorCloud GPU endpoints for 8k-context chat at 4k-token responses" — compare price-per-1M-tokens at steady-state throughput.
- Claim C (product differentiator): "Automatic prefix caching reduces cold-start visible latency by 60% on common chat patterns" — validated via synthetic replay of 50k sessions.

Hypotheses to validate (experimental framing):
1) SLO->pricing alignment increases conversion for platform teams evaluating dedicated/reserved capacity. (Measure: lead-to-opportunity conversion pre/post pilot messaging)
2) Presenting p95 latency + unit cost per 1M tokens reduces objections around cost unpredictability. (Measure: objection rate in sales calls)
3) Batching + KV cache delivers >20% token-cost reduction without violating p95 SLO for common workloads. (Measure: cost delta in benchmark runs)

Benchmarks / evidence matrix (high level):
- Inputs: model variant (redwood-v1-small, v1-medium), hardware profiles (A100-80G, H100-80G), sequence distributions (short chat: 16-64 tokens; long context: 512-8k tokens), concurrency (1, 8, 32), burst patterns (steady vs spiky).
- Metrics to capture: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (request and per-token), throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, memory footprint, cost-per-1M-tokens (normalized).
- Acceptance thresholds (for claim staging):
  * Internal-experiment pass: median and p95 within 10% of claim on 3 runs
  * Customer-staging pass: single customer workload replay with p95 within claim and <5% higher cost than internal lab run

Test plan (short checklist):
- [ ] Define 6 canonical workload traces (3 chat, 2 embeddings/rerank, 1 long-context completion). Owner: Arjun.
- [ ] Run baseline on MajorCloud equivalent endpoints (public pricing snapshot). Owner: Derek.
- [ ] Internal Redwood runs across hardware profiles (A100/H100 + quantized variants). Owner: Perf Eng.
- [ ] Run KV-cache ON/OFF experiments and record delta. Owner: Maya + Perf Eng.
- [ ] Collect economic normalization table (incl. reserved capacity amortization assumptions). Owner: Finance liaison (Sophie).
- [ ] Draft customer-facing claims and legal-ready claim guardrails. Owner: GTM counsel + Maya.

Messaging snippets (customer-facing drafts — for website/one-pager/sales):
- Headline: "Predictable latency, predictable cost — SLO-backed serving for production LLMs"
- Subhead: "Reduce per-token spend while guaranteeing the latency your users expect."
- Bullet-style proof point: "p95 <= 250ms for common conversational flows on Dedicated; typical token cost 20% lower than public GPU endpoints once prefix caching & batching are enabled."
- Short sales opener: "We benchmarked three customer traces and reduced visible latency by 40% while improving token economics; can we run one of your traces next week to show you?"

Guardrails / legal notes (what marketing can't claim without evidence):
- Avoid absolute comparatives without explicit test conditions ("faster than X" must include model, context length, concurrency).
- Don't mix host pricing vs reserved capacity without normalization table.
- Any claim including percent improvement vs competitor must have reproducible benchmark steps attached in linked artifact PR.

Competitive frame (rough notes for battlecard):
- MajorCloud: strong pole position on model catalog; weakness = opaque SLOs and per-request cost variability under burst. Opportunity: claim predictability and SLO guarantees for reserved/dedicated tiers.
- VendorOpaque: can be cheaper at extremely high batch sizes but requires deep ops investment; positioning: "single API + autoscaling policies reduces ops cost and keeps token economics stable".
- OpenServe variants: tradeoffs around quantization and throughput; claim angle: "we provide quantization recommendations + cost forecasts tied to your workload, not just a catalog of models."

Sample sales pitch flow (short):
1) Ask about user latency SLOs ("What p95 do you need for chat to feel smooth?").
2) Share our SLO-backed tier and a benchmark snippet (p95 | cost per 1M tokens for similar workload).
3) Offer a 72-hour customer trace replay to give a tailored SLO & cost projection.

Metrics to report regularly to GTM (dashboard suggestions):
- Number of leads requesting trace replay
- Conversion rate after SLO pitch
- Average delta between internal bench and customer staging
- Frequency of "cost unpredictability" objections logged in CRM

Open questions / notes to self:
- How to show amortized reserved-capacity cost vs on-demand public endpoints in a single clean graphic? (Finance input needed)
- Decide default context-length to use for web homepage claim (short: 256 tokens? 512?).
- Need legal checklist for comparative claims — copy of precedent from previous campaigns.

Next steps & owners (immediate):
- Maya: consolidate benchmark scripts into PR and tag perf team. (ETA: 2026-02-20)
- Arjun: finalize canonical workloads and upload traces. (ETA: 2026-02-16)
- Sophie: produce cost normalization worksheet and one-pager for sales. (ETA: 2026-02-23)
- Derek: run competitor public endpoint runs and share raw data. (ETA: 2026-02-18)

Appendix: example normalized unit-econ formula (working):
- normalized_cost_per_1M = (cloud_unit_price * effective_tokens) * (1 - batching_gain) * (1 - cache_hit_rate * cache_gain) + amortized_reserved_fee_per_1M
- note: batching_gain and cache_gain are experimentally measured; amortized_reserved_fee uses 12-month commit assumption by default.

Rough estimated numbers (work-in-progress; do not publish):
- Typical chat trace (256 context, 64 response): p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 210ms on H100 dedicated under concurrency=8; normalized token cost ~ $18 per 1M tokens (with cache+batching).
- Public endpoint baseline (MajorCloud public SKU): p50 ~ 70ms, p95 ~ 400ms; token cost ~ $22 per 1M tokens under equivalent normalization.

If you're reading this mid-review: please add objections you hear in the field to the linked JIRA ticket so we can iterate on the claim wording.

---
Comments: intentionally experimental doc. We want to be conservative on public claims but aggressive on sales experiments.
